![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274391/assets/c9b2c979ee7356d3c8b638ad46cef3733d6c0db70965f1deec24413c5bf2136e.png)

Which of the diagrams shown above represent subspaces of ${R}^{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each diagram in turn.

- Diagram I does not represent a subspace. The vector $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ belongs to the given subset. But 

$$
2\cdot a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

lies outside the subset.

- Diagram II represents a set that does not contain the origin. But every subspace must contain the origin, so Diagram II is not a subspace of ${R}^{2}.$

- Diagram III does not represent a subspace.  In this case we have that the vector $a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ lies inside the given subset. But 

$$
(-1)\cdot a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

lies outside the subset.

So, the correct answer is "None".
